messages:
From: Susan Li <susan.li@novushealth.com>

Cc: ops@novushealth.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production latency spike — immediate assistance required

Rafael,

We just started seeing a sustained latency and error-rate spike for our production traffic hitting us-west-2 (AZ us-west-2a). Since 08:50 PST requests have a mix of 5xxs (~3.8%) and median tail latency moving from ~120ms to 1.2s. Throughput for our critical endpoint /v1/generate dropped ~40% over the last 20 minutes. This is impacting our patient-facing flows.

Attached logs (novus_latency_logs_1127.zip) and a screenshot of 500s. Our SREs have limited visibility into Redwood's internal routing — please advise immediate mitigation steps and estimated time to stabilization.

We need either:
- rapid routing out of us-west-2 for NovusHealth traffic (canary then ramp), or
- confirmation of local mitigation timeline and a firm ETA.

Also escalate to your execs — if this goes >30m we will request contractual credits.

Susan Li
Director, Infrastructure
NovusHealth

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>

Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike — immediate assistance required

Susan — thanks for the heads up and the logs. We've kicked off an internal P0 bridge and our on-call is investigating. Initial read: pronounced queueing on the us-west-2a inference pool (in-flight KV cache pressure causing CPU backpressure on the serving nodes).

Immediate containment plan (proposal):
1) Start a controlled 5% canary redirect of NovusHealth traffic from us-west-2 -> eu-west-1 to relieve the AZ queue.
2) If canary shows error-rate drop and tail latency improvement after 10 minutes, ramp to 30% and then 100% in 20m increments with monitoring gates.
3) During canary we will perform a KV cache invalidation and bump batch size for affected model variant to reduce per-token queuing.

We need executive sign-off for cross-region routing (customer data flow policy + potential egress) and authorization to issue up to 10% credit if the outage continues beyond 60 minutes. Hannah — can you validate the cache-invalidation steps and estimated rollback time? Rishi — confirm no billing/regulatory blockers for NovusHealth traffic in eu-west-1. Vanessa — please pull the SLA and ML model pin for this tenant.

I will keep Susan and ops looped with timeline updates every 10 minutes.

— Rafael
SVP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

--

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:24:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Production latency spike — immediate assistance required

Quick technical notes:
- Root cause (hot-path): KV cache saturation + larger-than-expected prefix reuse for NovusHealth’s primary workload. This causes continuous re-population work and spikes CPU on the serving group in us-west-2a, which then backs up the request queue.
- Containment steps validated: start canary at 5% with sticky session preservation (we will forward x-api-tenant header so downstream remains routable). Canary will use the pre-provisioned eu-west-1 pool that has compatible model variant (quantized v2).
- Risks: cross-region introduces ~30–50ms additional RTT; some KV-layer warm-up likely requires a 5–15m tail before we see full improvement. We need to flush the local KV state for canaried traffic to avoid cache pollution — will run invalidation job in waves.
- Rollback: disable redirects and flush canary session cookies; estimated full rollback < 7m.

I'll attach the trimmed log set showing the queue length and a diff of p99 prior to spike. ETA to spin canary routing and start traffic shift: 12 minutes from now.

— Hannah (on-call)
